arrange.metrics: An explicit admitted deterministic metrics capability: each glyph including space advances s points and every line is s points high at candidate size s. No kerning or fallback. Each five-letter word fits at all candidates up to 18.

This is a security mapping, not a claim of renderer equivalence.

adaptation_rules.fixtures: Author the smallest valid owner graph in memory. Do not copy source decks, snippets, fonts, images or default templates. Preserve each numeric/enum/null/empty/control-character boundary; use original labels and authored bytes with the required metadata.
adaptation_rules.assertions: Use the declared neutral SDK model members and the corrected typed command route. Check observable return values, owned state, serialization and typed errors. Source assertion expressions are research oracles, not instructions to reproduce private classes.
adaptation_rules.mocks: Replace constructor/descriptor/mock-call expectations with observable returned interfaces, owner identity, mutation scope, relation targets and serialized state. Private call counts alone do not establish public parity; document the replacement for each retained expectation.
adaptation_rules.io: Use admitted Uint8Array/byte-source or explicit memfs-backed VFS capabilities. Await factories, save and binary admission even for in-memory bytes. No downloads, host reads, ambient time/fonts, process execution or product network.
adaptation_rules.commands: Retain model snake_case; operation JSON uses camelCase and dotted IDs. Use images, tables, properties, text replace, schema and capabilities. Whole-text assignment is an explicit resource setter. CLI positions are one-based; SDK sequences are zero-based and placeholders keyed.
adaptation_rules.deferred: An unresolved observable replacement is a case-specific open obligation. Neither a source pass nor an assigned task counts as an adapted or passing TypeScript test. Unsupported public behavior stays visible and blocks full parity.

documentation_findings.finding: J05 incorrectly described the pinned parser as slicing the first six characters. It parses the whole suffix from index four.
